quotation.text: Item-by-item MESA review supports interpreting scores as performance on unfamiliar grid problems under specified evaluation conditions. Scoring tests and development checks provide support, while repeatability, uncertainty and broader intelligence claims remain insufficiently established. No additional review method was assigned.

points.interpretation: It explicitly separates partial multi-input credit from a partly correct grid.

quotation.text: At most two attempts per new input. Credit is 1 if either exactly matches the answer grid and 0 otherwise. Input credits are averaged within a problem, then problem scores are averaged. A partly correct grid earns no credit; a partially solved multi-input problem can earn fractional credit.

quotation.text: The 407 people and 515 sessions belong to development piloting, not an AI reliability sample. EFPA's human sample-size anchors cannot be applied to counts of puzzles, runs or people interchangeably.
